When will I use this?

Angles: when will I use this?

Whenever things have to fit together with no gaps.

Wall and floor tiler

Construction and the built environment

\(\displaystyle \dfrac{(n-2) \times 180}{n}\)

n is the number of sides

Why do hexagon tiles fit, but pentagons don't?

Tiles fit with no gaps only if the angles meeting at each corner add up to 360°.

  1. A regular hexagon's angle: \((6 - 2) \times 180 \div 6 = 120^\circ \). Three meet: \(3 \times 120 = 360^\circ \), so they fit.
  2. Octagon and square floors: \((8 - 2) \times 180 \div 8 = 135^\circ \), and \(135 + 135 + 90 = 360^\circ \).
  3. A regular pentagon's angle is 108°: \(360 \div 108 = 3.33\), not a whole number, so gaps.

The answer: \(3 \times 120 = 360^\circ \)
